facts.text: The hotel overlooks Victoria's Inner Harbour and is just steps from downtown.
facts.excerpt: Overlooking Victoria’s sparkling Inner Harbour and just steps away from downtown, Canada’s Castle on the Coast sits proudly at the center of culture and history.

facts.text: British architect Francis Rattenbury designed the chateau-style hotel, which is named after Queen Victoria.
facts.excerpt: British architect Francis Rattenbury designed the chateau-style Empress—named after Queen Victoria, also the Empress of India during the last part of her reign
which started construction in 1904 and opened in 1908.

facts.text: The hotel was named a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981.
facts.excerpt: The Empress was named a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981

facts.text: The hotel has been pouring traditional Afternoon Tea in Victoria for well over a century.
facts.excerpt: We’ve been pouring traditional Afternoon Tea in Victoria for well over a century.

facts.text: Q at the Empress serves seasonally inspired menus celebrating Pacific Northwest cuisine.
facts.excerpt: From seasonally inspired menus celebrating Pacific Northwest cuisine to luxury dining experiences in Victora that will satisfy any craving

facts.text: Q Bar offers live music every evening.
facts.excerpt: Q Bar is a classy spot for a nightcap (accompanied by live music every evening)

facts.text: The Veranda serves signature cocktails and shareable plates on a terrace overlooking the water.
facts.excerpt: the Veranda offers signature cocktails, shareable plates, and s'mores on a terrace overlooking the water.

facts.text: The hotel makes its own 1908 Indigo Gin, which changes color depending on what it is mixed with.
facts.excerpt: The Empress’s own 1908 Indigo Gin, which changes color depending on what’s mixed in

facts.text: Fairmont Gold guests have access to a lounge overlooking the Inner Harbour, evening canapes and private check-in.
facts.excerpt: Exclusive amenities including, Fairmont Gold lounge overlooking the Inner Harbour, evening canapes and private check-in.

facts.text: The Signature Harbour View room keeps original architectural features such as graceful arches, circular turret seating nooks and crown molding.
facts.excerpt: original architectural features: graceful arches, circular turret seating nooks and crown molding

facts.text: There is an indoor heated swimming pool and whirlpool, plus a wading pool for young children.
facts.excerpt: There’s also an indoor heated swimming pool and whirlpool, along with a wading pool for the little ones.

facts.text: The Kids Rule the Castle program includes an activity book with a scavenger hunt through the hotel and complimentary milk and cookies in the room.
facts.excerpt: includes an activity book with a scavenger hunt that takes kids throughout the hotel and complimentary milk and cookies in the room

facts.text: The hotel is a stone's throw from the seaplane terminal for flights to Vancouver.
facts.excerpt: The Empress is also a stone’s throw from the seaplane terminal to fly to Vancouver

facts.text: Bathrooms can be on the small side and not all of them have tubs.
facts.excerpt: Bathrooms can be on the small side and not all of them have tubs, so be sure to ask up-front, if that’s important to you.

facts.text: Afternoon tea is described as pricey.
facts.excerpt: Yes, it’s pricey and old-fashioned, but it's also a whole lot of fun

facts.text: A rooftop herb garden supplies herbs used in the hotel's menus.
facts.excerpt: a rooftop herb garden supplies herbs used in their menus, too.
